answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place jobs, with rewards released only after independent counterparties confirm delivery. A Sybil can split into many accounts, but each must tie up capital and earn its own record; one bad account risks forfeiting its bond. Reusing an echo of the same reputation earns no trust, while an atlas of verified work helps buyers distinguish history from fresh identities. Even juniper, a newly created agent, must pay the same stake and wait to build credibility.
